subject: Clara Health — model fit assessment & guardrail plan (post-demo recap)
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Clara Torres <clara.torres@clarahealth.org>, Dr. Elena Ruiz <e.ruiz@claraconsult.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clara Health — model fit assessment & guardrail plan (post-demo recap)

Hi Clara / Elena —

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion and very helpful context on the two use cases (nurse triage assistant + patient intake summarization). Quick recap and recommended next steps so we all have alignment: 

Summary of needs we captured:
- Sensitive PHI handling (structured + free text) with retention rules and audit logging.
- High refusal accuracy on disallowed content and strong, deterministic refusal language.
- Latency target ~350ms p99 for short-length queries (avg 20–60 tokens).
- Expected steady-state volume ~12 QPS, spikes to 50 QPS during mornings.

Redwood recommended starting point (preliminary):
- Model candidates: Redwood-13B-pt (8-bit quant), and Falcon-40B-4bit for higher-quality summarization.
- Safety profile: run refusal/regression suite focused on PHI leakage, impersonation, and hallucination on medications.
- Quantization + batching profile: 8-bit for latency, 4-bit for heavier summarization jobs.

Deliverables we can send in 48 hours: 
1) Prompt set & evaluation harness (seed prompts + expected outputs) — attached.
2) Baseline benchmark run (truthfulness, refusal rate, latency) with short summary of tradeoffs — link to results.
3) Sensitivity matrix mapping user flows to required guardrails and recommended enforcement points (prompt-level vs platform-level).

Requests for you before we run the baseline: 
- A redacted sample of the worst-case PHI examples you want the model to refuse or redact (we can accept CSV).
- Clarify whether summaries must be free of clinical interpretation (i.e., strictly descriptive) or if light clinical normalization is allowed.

Proposed next steps / timeline: 
- Clara: share redacted samples and confirm summary policy by end of week (Fri 3/5).
- Redwood: run baseline eval and share a one-page comparison by Tue 3/9.
- Schedule a 60-min POC planning call the week of 3/15 to select the pilot cohort.

Attachments: initial-prompt-sets.csv, sensitivity-matrix.xlsx

Thanks — happy to jump on another call if helpful.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

--
Note: If you prefer we can run the baseline inside a private VPC instance for PHI-sensitive samples; flag in reply and we'll set up the private ingest channel.

Subject: Re: Clara Health — model fit assessment & guardrail plan (post-demo recap)

Hi Hannah —

Appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 
- Redacted samples: I'll send a CSV with 200 de-identified rows (we'll mark fields that must be redacted vs. those that can be summarized). Expect in your inbox by EOD Thu 3/4.
- Clinical interpretation: for pilot we want summaries to be descriptive only (no diagnostic or prescriptive language). We may expand later if performance allows.
- SLA: we need an initial uptime target and RTO notes for the pilot (we've attached SLA_requirements.pdf).
- Compliance: would prefer the baseline to run inside a private VPC; PHI handling is non-negotiable.

I've attached the redaction guidelines and a short list of edge-case examples we worry about — these are illustrative, not exhaustive. Let us know if the format works.

Thanks,
Clara Torres
Director of Product, Clara Health
clara.torres@clarahealth.org | +1 (646) 555-0210

Subject: Re: Clara Health — model fit assessment & guardrail plan (post-demo recap)

Clara / team —

Thanks for the notes and the redaction file — that format will work for our pipeline. A couple of pragmatic recommendations from the model/eval side before we start the baseline run: 

1) Candidate model strategy (fast path vs quality path):
   - Fast path: Redwood-13B-8bit (lower latency, good refusal behavior with prompt engineering).
   - Quality path: Falcon-40B-4bit (better abstractive summarization, slightly higher cost + latency).
   - Fallback policy: route >1k-token inputs and long summarizations to the quality path; keep short triage queries on the fast path.

2) Safety/refusal evals we will run:
   - PHI leakage test (redacted-original vs model output) — recall and precision metrics.
   - Refusal accuracy test using adversarial prompts (we'll provide the suite).
   - Policy regression checks vs historical prompts (we'll baseline against our internal safety model v202702).

3) Guardrail approach:
   - Prompt-level hard refusals for explicit disallowed asks (templates + canned refusal language).
   - Platform-level post-filtering for entities tagged as high-risk (PHI tokens).
   - Audit trail: token-level logging + sample retention policy for any flagged outputs.

4) Quick POC proposal (2 weeks):
   - Week 1: baseline runs on your redacted CSV + initial refusal/regression report.
   - Week 2: implement prompt-level guardrails and rerun targeted probes; provide remediation guidance.

I've attached a short note with model-selection rationale and expected cost delta between the two paths. If Clara confirms private VPC, we'll provision a constrained environment and share an ingest endpoint.

Attachments: model-recommendations.md

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Applied ML Solutions | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
